_comment: Meeting scenes of the vignettes, letter c (Expansion 6 C.9; situations.vignettes_c.json meetings v_...).

vig_barrow_dog.about: A dog sits in the lane, and will not cross its own master's step, however it is called; the master, ashamed and afraid, comes over to you.

call: Here! Here, you! Come on, you daft thing!
Come in! Come in out of the lane! Come!
Here, girl. Here. It is only the house. It is only the house.
Please. Come on. Come in. It is cold.
bad: It will not cross the step. Not since the ring.
Three weeks it has slept in the lane, looking at the house.
Look at it. Just sat there. Looking past me, into the house.
open: You. You are not from here. Do you know anything of graves?
Stranger. A word. It is about the barrow at {barrow}.
Please. You look like someone who has seen worse than a dog.

vig_last_hearth.about: An old one tells children the night {ruin_was} fell, word for word, and stops when the children ask what came after; then looks up and sees you.

ask: Tell the part with the dog.
tell: We all ran together. We all ran together out of {ruin_was}, every one, and we did not look back.
It was the night {ruin_fall}. We all ran. My mother, and my brother, and I. Together.
Every one of us ran. I have the whole of it. I have it by heart.
stop: ...That is all. That is the end of it. Go home.
What came after? ... Nothing. Nothing came after. Go on, go home.
That is enough for today. Go home. Off.
open: You. You are a walker. You walk the roads.
Stranger. You go to the old places, I think. I can see it on you.
I have been watching you. You are the kind who goes where the roads end.

vig_beggar_row.about: A beggar and the notable of the town have words on the square, and the notable laughs; the beggar sees you and comes over.

row: The house on the square is mine. It was my people's before it was yours. The founders' blood is in me.
The founders' blood! Look at the state of you. Go and beg at the gate where the beggars beg.
Ask the rolls. Ask anyone who can read.
I do not need to ask a roll. I know whose house it is. Go on. Off the square.
open: You heard that. You heard all of it. Do not tell me you did not.
Stranger. You stood and listened. Then you know it is not nothing.
They laugh. They have laughed all my life. But you listened. Come here.

vig_page_nine.about: People nudge each other as someone passes; a boy spits on the ground at their feet; the one passing does not answer, and then turns to you.

murmur: It is written down, so it is true.
His grandfather. Or hers. The one who sold us.
Not a word, mind. Not in front of the children.
They say it is in the hall, in the big book.
ignore: I will not answer. I will not answer. Walk.
Let them. Let them say it.
It is a long time since I wept in the street.
open: You are not from here, so you have not heard it. Hear it from me before you hear it from them.
Stranger. You were watching. You saw what they do. Come here.
A word. It is about a book. I will not keep you.

vig_pilgrim_kneels.about: A pilgrim kneels at the side of the road and prays toward {shrine}, coughing between the words; people go round; the pilgrim rises, with difficulty, and comes to you.

murmur: That one will not see it.
pray: {shrine}, hear me. I am coming. Wait for me.
I am coming. I am coming. Do not close the door before I come.
Hold the lamp for me at {shrine}. I will be there. I will be there.
open: You. You are walking. Which way do you walk?
Stranger, you have good legs. I saw you come up the road.
Do not go by. I have something for someone who is going the right way.

vig_empty_room.about: A guest comes out of the inn at dusk with a pack on a shoulder, white-faced, and will not be stopped; the innkeeper runs after, then sees you.

stay: Wait! The bed is paid for, you have not even slept!
Do not go! It is only a draught. Only a draught!
Half the price, then! Half! Come back, come back!
mutter: Third this month. Third this month.
Nothing wrong with the house. Nothing at all.
They will sleep in the stable before they sleep in that room.
open: You, there. Are you staying in {town}? Do you need a bed?
Stranger. I will give you the best bed in the house, free. Hear me out.
You do not look like someone who is frightened of dark rooms.

vig_door_to_door.about: The priest goes down the street with two of the watch, knocking at every door and having it opened; the one at the next door watches, and when the priest has passed, crosses to you.

knock: Open your doors. By the bishop's letter, open your doors.
Open, in the name of the church. We search every house in the street.
Open. Nobody will be harmed who has nothing to hide.
murmur: They say there is a book.
I have nothing. I have nothing at all.
Not my door. Please. Not my door.
hush: Not here. Not here, in the street. Walk with me.
They are one door down. Quiet.
open: You are a stranger. Strangers are not searched. Listen.
I need someone nobody knows. You are the only one.
Look at me as though I were asking the time.
